rule: For each colour-1 blob, a stub of h lines of non-background, non-1 colours attached to one side, if it stops short of the border, is repeated periodically with period h outward to the border, overwriting anything in its path. Strips that already reach the border are left unchanged.
scope: Extend periodic striped stubs attached to blue blobs to the border; already-fired strips stay unchanged except where crossed by an extending stub. Random canvases 10..30, requested 6..30, exact one to four blobs, rectangles/rounded rectangles, four directions, one to three-line periods and optional stripless distractors.

authored_scope: Supported: background fixed at 8 and blob colour fixed at 1. Grids are 6..30 per side when requested and 10..30 by default; sizes other than the fixture sizes are synthetic extensions. Scenes hold 1..4 blobs, limited by grid size. Blobs are rounded rectangles (3..5 per side) or full rectangles (2..3 per side). There is at least one unfired stub of 1..3 lines; there may also be fired periodic strips (sometimes with an irregular tail) and stripless distractor blobs. Extensions may cross fired strips. Stub colours come from {2,3,4,5,6,7,9}. Not supported: several strips on one blob, overlapping or adjacent extensions, extensions that run into other blobs or live stubs, other background colours, and irregular (non-rectangle-derived) blob shapes.
authored_constraints: Input objects (a blob plus its strip) are separated by at least one background cell, including diagonally.
Every unfired stub has a line of input background immediately beyond it, so stub reading stops exactly at h.
Unfired stubs have minimal period equal to their length, so periodic-continuation readings cannot be confused.
Extensions never touch, even diagonally, another blob, another unfired stub or another extension. They may only cross fired strips.
Fired strips run exactly to the border.
Background 8 strictly outnumbers twice the count of any other colour in the input.
Every random scene has at least one extension, so the output differs from the input.
The requested num_objects is produced exactly or rejected up front if infeasible for the grid size.
